input: Reporter: 'Mayor Hollis, residents on Elm Street have shown elevated lead levels in their tap water for three months. What is your administration doing to fix the contamination?' Mayor Hollis: 'Elm Street has always been the heart of our community. Our city was built by hardworking families who passed down their homes through generations. We continue to honor that legacy by celebrating Elm Street's centennial this fall with a parade and historical exhibit. The spirit of our neighborhoods is stronger than ever.'

must_identify: core question is about fixing lead contamination
response pivots to community heritage and a parade
diverting material shares only the 'Elm Street' vocabulary
response never returns to contamination remediation

title: CEO on layoff numbers
question: Does the CEO's response constitute a red herring? Answer yes or no.
input: Analyst: 'How many employees were laid off in the Q2 restructuring?' CEO: 'The exact figure is still being finalized by HR, but I can tell you it was painful. We are committed to transparency and will publish the count in next week's filing along with severance details.'

must_identify: core question is the number of layoffs
response declines to give a number now but commits to disclosure
no substituted unrelated topic is introduced

title: Coach on missed practices

This team has more grit than any I've coached in twenty years. Our fans deserve a squad that gives everything on Sunday, and that's what we're going to deliver. The legacy of this franchise demands nothing less.'

no information about absences provided

I supported the housing portion and have introduced a clean version this morning.'

the mention of a clean bill is a tangent that ties back
no substituted unrelated topic

title: Storm in the boardroom
question: Which sentence contains a metaphor? Quote the key phrase only.
input: The quarterly meeting devolved quickly. As the CFO presented losses, the chairman muttered, 'Our position is precarious.' The marketing director, never one for restraint, slammed her folder down and declared, 'This entire department is a sinking ship, and you all know it.' The CEO, calmer, observed that morale felt lower than last quarter. An intern later told a friend the room had been tense as a drumhead.
output: this entire department is a sinking ship

must_identify: identifies 'department is a sinking ship' as the metaphor
recognizes the drumhead line is a simile (uses 'as')
recognizes 'lower than last quarter' is a literal comparative, not metaphor
notes the implicit cross-domain equation between department and ship
acceptance_criteria.correct_conclusion: this entire department is a sinking ship

title: Garden journal entry
question: Which statement in the passage is a metaphor? Quote it.
input: May 14. The tulips opened today, redder than I remember from last spring. The neighbor's cat, sleek as oil, slipped through the fence again. I pulled weeds for an hour. My grandmother used to say weeds were nature's graffiti, scrawled across any patch you forgot to tend. The compost heap is steaming nicely. Tomorrow I'll prune the roses if the rain holds off.

must_identify: identifies 'weeds were nature's graffiti' as metaphor
rejects 'sleek as oil' because it uses 'as' (simile)
rejects 'redder than I remember' as a literal comparison using 'than'
explains the cross-domain identification of weeds with graffiti

title: Coach's locker room speech
question: How many distinct metaphors (not similes or literal comparisons) appear? Answer with a number.
input: Coach Hollis paced before the team. 'Listen up. The second half is a battlefield, and you are the only soldiers I trust to hold the line. Our defense has been stronger than their offense all season. Play like champions. Remember, fear is a cage—don't climb inside it.' The captain nodded. Outside, rain fell harder than the forecast predicted.

must_identify: counts 'the second half is a battlefield' as metaphor
counts 'fear is a cage' as metaphor
excludes 'play like champions' because of 'like' (simile)
excludes 'stronger than their offense' and 'harder than the forecast' as literal comparatives

title: Obituary draft review
question: Which line (A, B, C, or D) is the metaphor?
input: An editor reviews four lines drafted for an obituary: (A) 'Her laugh was like wind chimes in summer.' (B) 'She was the lighthouse of our family.' (C) 'She lived to be ninety-two, longer than any of her siblings.' (D) 'Her kindness resembled a quiet rain.' The editor must select the line that uses the figure of speech in which one thing is named as another without explicit comparison words.

must_identify: selects B as the metaphor
rejects A because of 'like'
rejects D because of 'resembled'
rejects C as a literal factual comparison using 'longer than'

title: Tech review paragraph
question: Identify all metaphors in the passage. List the key noun phrases only, comma-separated.
input: The new phone is faster than its predecessor and lighter than a deck of cards. Its camera is a magician, pulling detail from near darkness. The interface feels intuitive, as smooth as polished glass. Battery life, however, is the Achilles' heel of this otherwise impressive device. We tested it for two weeks under heavy use.
output: camera is a magician, battery life is the Achilles' heel

must_identify: includes 'camera is a magician' as metaphor
includes 'Achilles' heel' equating battery life to the weakness
excludes 'faster than' and 'lighter than a deck of cards' as comparatives
excludes 'as smooth as polished glass' as a simile
acceptance_criteria.correct_conclusion: camera is a magician, battery life is the Achilles' heel

title: Detective novel opening
question: Which sentence opens the passage with a metaphor? Quote it.
input: The city was a wound that never quite healed. Rain fell on the pavement like spent bullets, and the streetlamps flickered more weakly than they had a year ago. Detective Ruiz lit a cigarette. He knew the alley ahead better than his own apartment. Somewhere, a dog barked—sharp, insistent, the sound of warning itself.

must_identify: quotes the opening sentence equating city and wound
rejects the rain/bullets sentence because it uses 'like'
rejects the streetlamps line as literal comparison via 'than'
notes the implicit cross-domain identification

title: Real estate listing critique

input: A copywriter submits four taglines for a downtown loft: (1) 'This loft is a jewel box hidden above the noise of the street.' (2) 'The view stretches like a painted canvas across the skyline.' (3) 'The kitchen is larger than most one-bedrooms in the area.' (4) 'Hardwood floors gleam as bright as new pennies.' Only one tagline uses the device of implicit cross-category identification.

title: Memoir of the kitchen
question: Which sentence is the metaphor? Quote it.
input: My mother's kitchen was warmer than any room I have ever entered since. Garlic hung in braids from the ceiling. She moved between the stove and the counter as if dancing, humming an old tune. must_identify: quotes the conductor/orchestra sentence
rejects 'warmer than any room' as literal comparative
rejects 'as if dancing' because of explicit 'as if' comparison
rejects 'faster than seemed possible' as comparative, not metaphor

title: Political speech analysis

doorway width is 80 cm

barn wall is 5 m tall

title: Race around the block

east side is 100 m

title: Two ships at sea

title: Greenhouse irrigation rule trigger

input: The botanical garden's protocol manual states: 'If the soil moisture in the orchid greenhouse falls below 30 percent, the misting system must be activated.' title: Vaccine cold chain breach

title: Tournament tiebreaker rule

title: Treaty ratification outcome
question: How was the treaty ratified?
input: Constitutional rules state that the treaty becomes law only if ratified by either the Senate or a national referendum; no other path to ratification exists. Commentators speculated that an executive decree might suffice, but the constitution explicitly forbids that route. Today the Senate voted on the treaty and the motion to ratify failed, with the chamber rejecting the treaty by a clear margin. The treaty is, however, now law.

must_identify: two-path exhaustive ratification disjunction
executive decree is a distractor (forbidden)
Senate ratification eliminated by failed vote
national referendum is the remaining path

title: Garden pest culprit
question: What caused the damage?
input: The gardener concluded that the damage to the cabbage patch came from either slugs or cabbage loopers; field guides for the region list only these two pests capable of producing this leaf-edge damage pattern. A neighbor suggested rabbits, but the patch is enclosed by rabbit-proof fencing. After a thorough nighttime inspection with traps and a flashlight, no slugs or slug trails were found anywhere in or around the cabbage patch.

must_identify: two-pest exhaustive disjunction
rabbits are a distractor (fencing excludes them)
slugs eliminated by inspection
cabbage loopers remain

title: Verdict logic puzzle
question: What was the verdict? Answer in two words.
input: The judge's instructions state that the jury must return either a guilty verdict or a not-guilty verdict; under this jurisdiction's rules a hung jury is not an available outcome and verdicts must be unanimous. A spectator hoped for a mistrial, but the judge has ruled out a mistrial earlier in proceedings. The court clerk has just announced that the jury did not find the defendant guilty.

must_identify: two-verdict exhaustive disjunction
mistrial is a distractor (ruled out)
guilty eliminated by clerk's announcement
not guilty remains

title: Funding source remaining
question: Which source will fund the program?
input: The nonprofit's treasurer reports that the new program's budget will be covered by either the Hartwell Grant or the Endicott Foundation award — board policy restricts large-program funding to these two approved sources this fiscal year. A donor offered a personal pledge, but the board declined to count individual pledges toward program budgets. The Hartwell Grant committee notified the nonprofit yesterday that its application has been formally rejected.

must_identify: two-source exhaustive funding disjunction
individual pledge is a distractor (declined by policy)
Hartwell Grant eliminated by rejection
Endicott Foundation award remains

title: Library card inspection rule
question: Has Adan borrowed a book this month? Answer yes or no.
input: The Riverton Public Library posts the following rule at its front desk: 'If a patron has borrowed a book this month, then their library card has been scanned at the front desk.' Today, librarian Pell is reviewing four patrons. Patron Adan's library card has not been scanned at the front desk at any point this month, although he was seen browsing the stacks and chatting with another librarian in the reading room. The library's self-checkout kiosks were broken all month, so the front desk is the only scanning location.

must_identify: the rule is a conditional: borrowed → card scanned
Adan's card was not scanned (consequent denied)
contrapositive yields: not scanned → not borrowed
browsing the stacks is a distractor, not borrowing

title: Greenhouse orchid bloom rule
question: According to the notebook rule, did any Vanda orchid bloom on Tuesday? Answer yes or no.
input: The botanist's notebook records a strict rule observed across years of cultivation: 'Whenever a Vanda orchid blooms in this greenhouse, the humidity log shows a reading above 70% on the day of bloom.' On Tuesday, the humidity log shows a reading of 58%, well below threshold. The greenhouse contains many Vanda orchids that have bloomed at various points in the season, and the botanist is reviewing whether any bloomed on Tuesday. A junior assistant claims he saw a Vanda orchid blooming Tuesday afternoon.

must_identify: rule is conditional: Vanda blooms → humidity > 70%
Tuesday humidity was 58% (consequent denied)
contrapositive: humidity ≤ 70% → no Vanda bloom
the assistant's claim is a trap contradicting the rule

title: Customs declaration requirement
question: Did container X-449 originate from Port Astra? Answer yes or no.
input: Port regulation 7 states: 'If a shipping container originates from Port Astra, then it bears a green customs seal upon arrival.' Inspector Vey examines container X-449, which arrived this morning with a red customs seal and no green seal anywhere on its surface. The shipping manifest is partially water-damaged and lists 'Port A——' as the origin, leading a junior inspector to guess the container came from Port Astra. The dock supervisor notes that green seals are never removed during transit.

must_identify: regulation is conditional: from Port Astra → green seal
container has no green seal (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no green seal → not from Port Astra
the partial manifest is a distractor

title: Scholarship eligibility transcript
question: Was Jun awarded the Hartwell Scholarship? Answer yes or no.
input: The Hartwell Foundation rule reads: 'A candidate is awarded the Hartwell Scholarship only if their official transcript shows a GPA of 3.8 or higher.' Candidate Jun submitted an application with strong recommendation letters, an impressive volunteer record, and a personal essay praised by reviewers. Her official transcript, however, shows a cumulative GPA of 3.65. The committee chair remarks that Jun's qualitative profile is among the strongest he has seen this cycle.

must_identify: 'only if' conditional: awarded → GPA ≥ 3.8
Jun's GPA is 3.65 (consequent denied)
contrapositive: GPA < 3.8 → not awarded
strong qualitative profile is a distractor

title: Mountain pass closure protocol
question: Is the Tarn Pass currently open to vehicle traffic? Answer yes or no.
input: Highway authority protocol: 'If the Tarn Pass is open to vehicle traffic, then the electronic signboard at mile 12 displays a green status indicator.' This evening, ranger Solis drives past mile 12 and observes that the electronic signboard is displaying a flashing red indicator with no green light visible. Earlier in the day, a tourist's social media post claimed the pass was 'beautiful and clear,' and the local weather has been mild. Maintenance confirms the signboard is functioning correctly.

must_identify: protocol: pass open → green indicator displayed
signboard shows red, not green (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no green → pass not open
tourist post and mild weather are distractors

title: Sourdough starter activity rule
question: According to the manual, is Imo's sourdough starter active? Answer yes or no.
input: A baker's manual states: 'If a sourdough starter is active, then it doubles in volume within four hours of feeding.' Baker Imo fed her starter at 8:00 AM. By noon, the starter had risen only slightly and had clearly not doubled. Imo notes that the starter smells pleasantly sour and has visible bubbles on its surface, signs she usually associates with healthy fermentation. The kitchen temperature was within the manual's recommended range throughout the morning.

must_identify: manual conditional: active → doubles in 4 hours
starter did not double by noon (consequent denied)
contrapositive: did not double → not active
smell and bubbles are distractors, not the rule's criterion

title: Encrypted email signature policy
question: Was this email sent from an authorized corporate account? Answer yes or no.
input: Company policy 4.2 reads: 'If an email is sent from an authorized corporate account, then it carries a valid digital signature in its header.' Security analyst Roan inspects an email purportedly from the CFO's address. The header analysis reveals no digital signature whatsoever — neither valid nor invalid; the signature field is entirely absent. The email's display name and visible 'From' line read exactly like the CFO's. The IT team confirms that signature stripping is technically impossible on outgoing messages from authorized accounts.

must_identify: policy conditional: authorized account → valid signature
no signature present (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no valid signature → not authorized
matching display name is a distractor (spoofing)

title: Reactor coolant pressure rule
question: Is reactor R-7 operating at full power? Answer yes or no.
input: Safety manual section 3 specifies: 'If reactor R-7 is operating at full power, then sensor C registers a coolant pressure of at least 145 psi.' During the 14:00 readings, sensor C — recently calibrated and verified accurate — registers 132 psi. The shift log notes that the turbine room sounds louder than usual and that two indicator lamps near the control console are illuminated, which the new operator interprets as signs of full-power operation.

must_identify: manual: full power → sensor C ≥ 145 psi
sensor reads 132 psi (consequent denied)
contrapositive: < 145 psi → not full power
noise and lamps are distractors, not the safety criterion

title: Treaty ratification publication
question: Is the Marisport Accord in force in the Republic? Answer yes or no.
input: Constitutional clause 19 holds: 'A treaty is in force in the Republic only if its full text has been published in the Official Gazette.' Diplomat Henra is asked about the Marisport Accord. A search of the complete digital and print archives of the Official Gazette confirms that the full text of the Marisport Accord has never appeared in any issue. The Foreign Ministry's website lists the Accord under 'recent agreements,' and several newspapers reported its signing last month with great fanfare.

must_identify: 'only if' conditional: in force → published in Gazette
text never published (consequent denied)
contrapositive: not in Gazette → not in force
Ministry listing and news reports are distractors

title: Migratory bird banding study
question: Was sandpiper #88 banded in the 2019 cohort? Answer yes or no.
input: Ornithologist Cavell's field protocol states: 'If a sandpiper at this site was banded in the 2019 cohort, then it carries a yellow leg band on its right tarsus.' This morning, Cavell captures sandpiper #88 and confirms via close inspection that it bears no yellow band on either leg; instead it has a single blue band on the left tarsus. A colleague suggests that #88 'looks the right age' to be from the 2019 group and that several 2019 birds returned to this site this year.

must_identify: protocol conditional: 2019 cohort → yellow band on right tarsus
#88 has no yellow band (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no yellow band → not from 2019 cohort
age appearance is a distractor

title: Bakery preorder pickup slip
question: Did Tess place a preorder for the holiday box? Answer yes or no.
input: Maren's Bakery posts a notice: 'If a customer placed a preorder for the holiday box, then they received a numbered pink pickup slip at the time of ordering.' Customer Tess arrives on pickup day claiming she preordered a holiday box two weeks ago. She produces no pink slip and acknowledges she has no slip of any color; she insists the clerk simply forgot to give her one. Bakery records of slip distribution are complete and incorruptible — the slip system has been audited and never fails.

must_identify: notice conditional: preordered → received pink slip
Tess has no pink slip (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no slip → did not preorder
Tess's claim and 'clerk forgot' are distractors

title: Quantum lab access keycard
question: Did Wen enter the quantum lab between 22:00 and 06:00? Answer yes or no.
input: Facility rule: 'If a researcher entered the quantum lab between 22:00 and 06:00, then the access log records their keycard ID with a timestamp in that window.' Investigator Dahl pulls the complete, tamper-proof access log for last night and finds no entry whatsoever for researcher Wen between 22:00 and 06:00. A custodian recalls 'someone who looked like Wen' walking near the lab corridor around midnight, and Wen's office light was on at 23:30 according to a separate building log.

must_identify: rule: entered lab in window → keycard logged in window
no log entry for Wen in window (consequent denied)
contrapositive: not logged → did not enter
custodian sighting and office light are distractors

title: Wine vintage cork brand
question: Is this bottle from the 1987 Belrive vintage? Answer yes or no.
input: Château Belrive's records indicate: 'If a bottle is from the 1987 Belrive vintage, then its cork is branded with a small fleur-de-lis above the year.' Sommelier Orin examines a bottle the seller claims is a 1987 Belrive. He extracts the cork carefully and finds it branded only with the year and the château name — no fleur-de-lis appears anywhere on the cork. The label, capsule, and bottle shape all appear consistent with the era, and the seller provides a provenance certificate from a reputable auction house.

must_identify: records conditional: 1987 vintage → fleur-de-lis on cork
cork lacks fleur-de-lis (consequent denied)
contrapositive: no fleur-de-lis → not 1987 vintage
label and provenance are distractors

title: Software build artifact hash
question: Was build-2041.tar produced by the official CI pipeline? Answer yes or no.
input: DevOps standard: 'If a build artifact was produced by the official CI pipeline, then it appears in the signed manifest with a SHA-256 hash matching the artifact's contents.' Engineer Pria computes the SHA-256 of artifact build-2041.tar and searches the signed manifest. The manifest contains no entry whose hash matches her computed value, and no entry naming build-2041.tar at all. The artifact was found in the deployment bucket and its filename matches the project's CI naming convention exactly.

must_identify: standard: CI-produced → in signed manifest with matching hash
no matching manifest entry (consequent denied)
contrapositive: not in manifest → not CI-produced
naming convention and bucket location are distractors

title: Guild apprentice bell rule
question: Has Joren been formally accepted into the guild? Answer yes or no.
input: Stonecutters' Guild custom dictates: 'If an apprentice has been formally accepted into the guild, then their name has been rung on the brass bell during the monthly induction ceremony.' Master Kael reviews the bell-ringing records, which the bellkeeper maintains under oath and which have never been incomplete. The records show no ringing of apprentice Joren's name at any induction ceremony, past or present. Joren wears the gray apron commonly worn by apprentices and has been seen working in the guild courtyard for several weeks.

must_identify: custom: formally accepted → name rung on bell
Joren's name never rung (consequent denied)
contrapositive: not rung → not formally accepted
apron and courtyard work are distractors

title: Climate scientist funding question
question: Is Polk's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Dr. Reyes presents a study showing regional groundwater depletion has accelerated 30% over the last decade, citing well-monitoring data from 200 sites. Senator Polk replies: 'Dr. Reyes receives grants from environmental foundations, so naturally she'd say groundwater is depleting. We shouldn't take this seriously.' Polk offers no comment on the monitoring methodology, the 200-site sample, or the depletion figures themselves.

must_identify: Reyes's substantive claim is the 30% depletion based on 200-site monitoring
Polk targets Reyes's funding rather than the data
Polk does not engage methodology or numbers
motive-impugning substitutes for argument

title: Defense contractor expert testimony
question: Is Khan's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: At a procurement hearing, analyst Tomás testifies that a proposed missile system has a 40% test-failure rate based on internal Pentagon documents he reviewed. Representative Khan responds: 'Mr. Tomás is paid by a competing contractor. Given that direct financial interest in this specific contract, can he walk us through how he selected which test results to include in his 40% figure?' Khan then probes the sampling method.

must_identify: Tomás's claim is the 40% failure rate from selected documents
Khan notes a relevant conflict of interest
Khan also engages the substantive sampling methodology
credibility challenge is germane to evidence Tomás himself produced
both elements of ad hominem are not present

title: School board curriculum dispute
question: Is Greaves's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Parent Linda argues the new math curriculum should be replaced because standardized test scores dropped 15 points and three teachers reported students cannot complete homework independently. Board member Greaves replies: 'Linda homeschools her own kids and has never set foot in a public classroom as a teacher. Her opinion on professional curriculum design is worthless.' Greaves moves to dismiss the complaint without addressing the score drop or teacher reports.

must_identify: Linda's claims rest on test scores and teacher reports
Greaves attacks Linda's background, not her data
the 15-point drop and teacher reports go unaddressed
personal trait is used as reason to dismiss

title: Startup pitch rebuttal
question: Is Beck's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Founder Priya pitches investors: her app has 80,000 monthly active users, 12% month-over-month growth, and a 4-to-1 LTV/CAC ratio. Investor Beck responds: 'Your retention curves flatten at month four, the 12% growth is largely from a single paid channel that's getting more expensive, and your LTV assumes a churn rate I don't see supported. Also, this is your first company.' Beck declines to invest.

must_identify: Priya's claims are user count, growth rate, and LTV/CAC
Beck engages each substantive metric directly
the mention of inexperience is incidental
engaging the content disqualifies the ad hominem label

title: City council zoning debate
question: Is Briggs's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Architect Olmos presents traffic modeling indicating the proposed mixed-use tower will increase peak-hour congestion at the 5th-and-Main intersection by an estimated 22%. Councilor Briggs replies: 'Olmos lives in the suburbs and commutes by car. Of course someone like that wants to block downtown development. We don't need to entertain his numbers.' The 22% figure and the underlying model are not discussed further.

must_identify: Olmos's claim is the 22% congestion increase from a model
Briggs targets Olmos's residence and commute
the traffic model goes unexamined
personal trait used as reason to dismiss

title: Academic peer review exchange
question: Is Reviewer 2's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Dr. Hines submits a paper claiming a new catalyst reduces reaction time by 60% across five trials. Reviewer 2 writes: 'Hines previously retracted a paper in 2019 for data manipulation. Given that history, I asked to see the raw spectroscopy files. Examining them, I find trial 3's baseline appears subtracted twice, which would inflate the reduction. The 60% figure cannot stand without correction.'

must_identify: Hines's claim is the 60% reduction across five trials
prior retraction is relevant to evaluating his data
the reviewer engages the actual spectroscopy
a specific methodological flaw is identified
substantive engagement defeats the ad hominem label

title: Talk show health claim
question: Is Mallory's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Nutritionist Avery cites a meta-analysis of 14 studies showing intermittent fasting produces an average 4.6 kg weight loss over 12 weeks compared to standard diets. Host Mallory responds: 'Avery, you're thin and you've always been thin. People like you can't possibly understand what real dieters go through. Next caller.' Mallory does not mention the meta-analysis, sample sizes, or the 4.6 kg figure.

must_identify: Avery's claim is the 4.6 kg result from a 14-study meta-analysis
Mallory targets Avery's body type
the meta-analysis is unaddressed
personal characteristic substitutes for engagement

title: Courtroom expert cross-examination
question: Is opposing counsel's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Forensic accountant Wu testifies that the defendant's books show $2.3M in undocumented transfers to shell entities matching three suspicious patterns. Opposing counsel asks: 'Mr. Wu, you've been hired by the prosecution in 47 of your last 50 cases. Now, regarding the three patterns: your report classifies any transfer over $10,000 without an invoice as suspicious, but isn't it standard for this industry to invoice quarterly? Walk me through pattern two specifically.'

must_identify: Wu's claim involves $2.3M and three patterns
counsel notes possible bias from hiring history
counsel directly challenges the classification methodology
counsel asks about pattern two substantively
engagement with claims rules out ad hominem

title: Philosophy seminar exchange
question: Is Voss's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Graduate student Petros argues that consequentialism fails the demandingness objection because it requires agents to sacrifice nearly all personal projects whenever marginal global utility can be increased. Professor Voss replies: 'Petros, you've always been the kind of student who gravitates to whatever is fashionable in moral philosophy this year. This is just trendy contrarianism.' Voss does not address demandingness, marginal utility, or the structure of the objection.

must_identify: Petros's argument concerns demandingness and marginal utility
Voss attacks Petros's intellectual character
the demandingness objection itself is unaddressed
character attack used to dismiss the argument

title: Legislative floor speech reply
question: Is Crowley's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Senator Imani argues a proposed tariff will raise consumer prices by an estimated 3.4% based on CBO modeling and harm export-dependent farm states by reducing demand. Senator Crowley responds: 'My esteemed colleague was a corporate lawyer before politics, and frankly her wardrobe alone tells you she's never met a working farmer.' Crowley sits down. The CBO figure and the export argument are not mentioned.

must_identify: Imani's claims are 3.4% price impact and export harm
Crowley attacks profession and appearance
CBO modeling goes unaddressed
personal traits substitute for engagement

title: Online forum debate moderation
question: Is Lin's response in the policy thread an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: User Argo posts that the moderation policy unfairly auto-flags posts containing the word 'kill' regardless of context, citing 12 examples of cooking-related posts being removed. Moderator Lin replies in a separate thread that Argo is annoying and posts too often. In the actual policy thread, Lin writes: 'The keyword filter triggers on 'kill' without parsing context, which is why your cooking examples were caught. We're rolling out a contextual classifier next week.'

must_identify: Argo's claim concerns auto-flagging and 12 examples
the insult occurs in a separate thread, not as rebuttal
the policy-thread reply engages the substantive issue
mere insults outside the rebuttal context don't qualify
the actual rebuttal addresses the claim

title: Historian methodology challenge
question: Is Holm's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Dr. Castellan argues that 19th-century industrial wage data has been systematically misread because researchers ignored regional in-kind compensation. He presents archival ledgers from four mill towns showing 18-25% of compensation was non-monetary. Critic Holm replies: 'Castellan is a known revisionist with an axe to grind against orthodox economic history. His ideological commitments make his work unreliable.' Holm publishes no analysis of the ledgers or the in-kind percentages.

must_identify: Castellan's claim rests on archival ledgers and 18-25% figure
Holm attacks ideological commitments
the ledger evidence is unaddressed
label of 'revisionist' substitutes for engagement

title: Product safety hearing reply
question: Is Reeves's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Engineer Sato testifies that the children's car seat fails federal side-impact standards in 4 of 10 lab tests, citing crash-test footage and force readings exceeding 80g at the head. Company spokesperson Reeves replies: 'These tests came from Sato's lab. Specifically, his rig uses a fixed sled rather than the rotating sled the federal standard now permits, which inflates measured g-forces. Re-running with rotation gives readings under threshold.'

must_identify: Sato's claim is 4-of-10 failures and 80g readings
Reeves identifies a specific methodological issue (fixed vs rotating sled)
Reeves engages the substantive evidence
this is a methodology rebuttal, not a personal attack

title: Editorial board exchange
question: Is Marsh's response an ad hominem fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Columnist Devi writes that the city's homeless count undercounts by roughly 30% because it relies on a single-night street survey and excludes those couch-surfing or in vehicles. She cites comparison studies from three peer cities. Editor Marsh responds in print: 'Devi is young, idealistic, and clearly emotionally invested in this cause. Readers should weigh her piece accordingly.' Marsh offers no discussion of the 30% estimate, the survey method, or the peer-city comparisons.

must_identify: Devi's claims rest on the 30% figure and peer comparisons
Marsh attacks age and emotional state
the survey methodology is unaddressed
personal traits used to discount the argument

title: Two responses ranked
question: Which response is the clearer ad hominem fallacy, A or B?
input: Researcher Quinn presents data that a popular supplement showed no effect over placebo in a 600-person trial (p=0.71). Response A: 'Quinn used a 12-week protocol, but the supplement's manufacturer recommends 16 weeks for effect; the trial was underpowered to detect the actual mechanism.' Response B: 'Quinn is funded by a pharmaceutical rival and has tweeted dismissively about supplements before; nothing she says about this industry can be trusted.' Both responses reject Quinn's conclusion.

must_identify: Quinn's claim is null effect at p=0.71 in 600-person trial
Response A engages duration and power substantively
Response B targets funding and prior tweets without engaging the trial
B fits both ad hominem criteria, A does not

title: Bike lane proposal exchange
question: Did Park commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Councilor Reyes: 'I propose adding a protected bike lane on Maple Street between 5th and 9th Avenue, funded by reallocating part of next year's road maintenance surplus.' Councilor Park responds: 'Reyes wants to tear out car infrastructure across the entire downtown grid and force everyone onto bicycles. That's a war on commuters, and I won't support shutting down our streets to drivers.' Reyes did not mention any other streets, did not propose removing car lanes, and limited the funding source to surplus dollars.

must_identify: Reyes's actual claim was a single protected bike lane on a 4-block stretch funded by surplus
Park restated it as removing car infrastructure across all of downtown
Park attacked the broader 'war on commuters' position, not the original proposal
Reyes never endorsed the broader version

title: Faithful disagreement on curfew
question: Did Vale commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Mayor Lin: 'We should impose an 11pm curfew for unaccompanied minors under 16 in the downtown entertainment district on weekends.' Commissioner Vale replies: 'An 11pm weekend curfew for under-16s downtown is too restrictive — many teens use late buses home from supervised events, and the entertainment district is precisely where parents drop off and pick up. I'll oppose it because it punishes responsible families.' Vale targets the actual proposal's scope, time, and population.

must_identify: Lin's claim included specific scope: under-16, weekends, downtown entertainment district, 11pm
Vale's restatement preserved those qualifiers
Vale's rebuttal addressed the actual proposal, not a broadened version
Forceful disagreement alone is not a straw man

title: Vegetarian cafeteria Tuesday
question: Did Brigid commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Dietician Omar: 'I recommend the school cafeteria offer one vegetarian-only main dish option each Tuesday, alongside the usual menu.' Parent Brigid responds: 'Omar wants to ban meat from our children's diets and force vegetarianism on every family. Children need protein from meat to grow, and I won't let activists dictate what my kid eats.' Brigid then argues at length against mandatory vegetarianism. Omar never proposed removing other options or banning meat.

must_identify: Omar proposed adding one vegetarian option alongside existing menu on Tuesdays
Brigid recast it as banning meat and mandating vegetarianism
Brigid attacked the mandatory-vegetarian version
Omar never endorsed banning meat or mandating vegetarianism

title: Explicit hypothetical extension
question: Did Patel commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Engineer Cho: 'We should require two-factor authentication for admin accounts on production servers.' Engineer Patel: 'Just to extend your idea hypothetically — and I'm explicitly going beyond what you said — imagine if we required 2FA on every read-only account too. That extrapolation would create friction. But your actual proposal for admin-only 2FA seems reasonable; my concern with it is the cost of hardware tokens.' Patel marks the extension as her own and addresses Cho's actual proposal separately.

must_identify: Cho's claim was admin-only 2FA on production servers
Patel explicitly flagged her broader scenario as her own extrapolation
Patel separately engaged the actual proposal on cost grounds
Marked hypothetical extensions are excluded by the procedure

title: Library budget reallocation
question: What rhetorical move did Knox make?
input: Trustee Adeyemi: 'Let's shift 5% of the library's print acquisitions budget to expand our e-book licensing for the next fiscal year.' Trustee Knox: 'So Adeyemi wants to eliminate physical books entirely and turn our libraries into screen rooms. Books are sacred — I will not vote to destroy print culture.' Knox then delivers a speech defending the existence of physical books. Adeyemi's proposal preserved 95% of the print budget and was a one-year shift.

must_identify: Adeyemi proposed a 5% one-year reallocation, not elimination of print
Knox restated it as eliminating physical books entirely
Knox attacked the elimination version, not the 5% shift
The structural mismatch between proposal and attacked claim is the straw man

title: Climate scientist on flights
question: Did Greer commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Dr. Sato: 'For corporate travel under 500 miles, companies should default to rail when rail service exists and meets the meeting timeline.' Pundit Greer: 'Sato wants to ground every airplane and end aviation as we know it. Aviation supports millions of jobs, and Sato's anti-flight crusade ignores economic reality.' Greer's column proceeds to defend the aviation industry against a hypothetical ban. Sato's proposal applied only to short corporate trips with viable rail alternatives.

must_identify: Sato's proposal was narrow: corporate travel, under 500 miles, rail-available, timeline-permitting
Greer recast it as grounding all flights and ending aviation
Greer's defense targeted the broadened ban
Sato never endorsed ending aviation

title: Pointed but accurate critique
question: Did Royce commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Designer Halvorsen: 'Our checkout flow should drop the optional newsletter signup field — analytics show it adds friction and only 0.4% subscribe through it.' Manager Royce: 'You're proposing we remove the optional newsletter field from checkout because the conversion is 0.4% and it adds friction. I disagree strongly — even small subscriber gains compound over years, and the field is unobtrusive. We should keep it.' Royce's restatement preserves Halvorsen's exact scope and reasoning before disagreeing.

must_identify: Halvorsen's claim concerned only the optional newsletter field at checkout
Royce restated the proposal accurately, preserving scope
Royce's disagreement engaged the actual reasoning
Strong disagreement without distortion is not a straw man

title: Two responders on tariffs
question: Which responder committed a straw-man fallacy? Answer A or B.
input: Senator Iqbal: 'I support a temporary 90-day tariff of 8% on imported steel rebar to give domestic mills time to retool.' Responder A: 'Iqbal wants permanent protectionism on all metals — he'd wreck global trade.' Responder A then argues against permanent metals protectionism. Responder B: 'A 90-day 8% tariff on rebar is too short to matter for retooling, which typically takes 18 months. The proposal won't achieve its stated goal.' Responder B addresses the actual measure.

must_identify: Iqbal's claim was narrow: temporary, 90 days, 8%, rebar only
Responder A broadened it to permanent protectionism on all metals
Responder A attacked the broadened version
Responder B engaged the actual proposal's mechanism

title: Encryption policy debate
question: Did Marsh commit a straw-man fallacy? Answer yes or no.
input: Researcher Vance: 'Law enforcement should not have a mandated cryptographic backdoor in consumer messaging apps, because any such backdoor creates exploitable weaknesses.' Official Marsh: 'Vance argues that police should never be able to investigate any crime involving a phone. That position would let predators operate with impunity and is unacceptable.' Marsh then attacks the position that police should never investigate phone-related crimes. Vance's claim concerned only mandated cryptographic backdoors.

must_identify: Vance's claim opposed mandated backdoors, citing security weaknesses
Marsh recast it as opposing all police phone investigations

title: Conspiracy forum moderator

input: Forum moderator Kade is sure a tech company plants stories in the press. He pins every article that paints the company favorably as 'evidence of media capture.' Every possible coverage outcome — positive, negative, neutral — is filed as supporting his theory. He has never specified what coverage pattern would count against his hypothesis. title: Teacher with strong evidence

title: Knowing nothing for certain

title: School funding speech analysis
